hints: Don't judge by how many digits a number has. Compare place by place.
Add zeros at the end so every number has 3 digits after the point. For example, 0.45 becomes 0.450.
With 3 digits after the point each, compare the digits after the point like whole numbers. The largest wins.

solution.methodName: Add zeros to the same length, then compare

steps.action: Give every number 3 digits after the point: 0.450, 0.500, 0.405 and 0.050.
steps.why: Zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value. ₱0.5 and ₱0.50 are the same amount.

steps.action: Compare the digits after the point like whole numbers: 450, 500, 405 and 50.
500 is the largest, so 0.500 is the largest.
steps.why: Another check: 0.5 has 5 tenths. 0.45 and 0.405 have only 4 tenths, and 0.05 has 0 tenths.

trapNotes.0.45: 45 looks bigger than 5, but 0.45 = 0.450, which is less than 0.500. More digits do not mean a bigger number.
trapNotes.0.405: This has the most digits, but it has only 4 tenths. 0.405 is less than 0.500.
trapNotes.0.05: This is 5 hundredths. The 0 right after the point means 0 tenths, so it is the smallest here.
